title: Digital Room visitor payload
description:
Attached by the Cognigy agent to a message as data._visitor, whenever it learns or updates who the visitor is. Deliberately a SIBLING of data._showroom rather than part of the stage directive: it says nothing about what is on the stage, and folding a non-stage concern into that contract would blur what the Stage is allowed to know.

The portal uses it to personalise the chrome, currently the company logo in the header. It is not required for any stage behaviour, and a client that ignores it must still work correctly.

v.description: Contract version. Ignore an unrecognised version rather than guessing.

company.description: As the visitor said it. Display only. NEVER use this to guess a domain or a logo: company names are ambiguous internationally, and a wrong guess puts a stranger's logo in a NiCE sales tool.

email.description: The authoritative company identifier is this address's domain, which is why no separate question is needed in the normal case.

website.description: Asked only when the email is a personal provider such as gmail, which identifies no employer. Takes precedence over the email domain when present, being the more deliberate signal.

audience.description: Who is actually in the room. Derived from the email domain, never asked directly. customer is an external visitor. nice-internal is a NiCE employee exploring for their own knowledge, for whom no CRM lookup happens at all. nice-on-behalf is a NiCE employee preparing for a named customer or prospect, in which case onBehalfOf carries that company and the conversation is conducted as if that company were the visitor.

onBehalfOf.description: Present only when audience is nice-on-behalf. The company the NiCE employee is preparing for, which becomes the subject of the CRM lookup, the header logo and the content targeting, in place of the employee's own employer. Without this the header would show the NiCE logo to a NiCE employee, which tells them nothing.

company.description: As the employee said it. Display only, never used to guess a domain.

website.description: The identifying signal, for the same reason as website above.

industry.description: The visitor's vertical, as one of the twelve labels in catalog/industries.json. Never a raw CRM string: Salesforce Industry holds well over a thousand distinct values in practice, so it is normalised at the boundary. Absent means we genuinely do not know, which is a normal outcome rather than an error.

industrySource.description: Where the vertical came from. crm means an account record answered; asked means CRM could not and the visitor chose from the buttons. Recorded for the same reason as typeSource on documents: a caller cannot otherwise tell a looked-up fact from a self-reported one, and they deserve different trust.

introductionComplete.description: True once the introduction questions are answered. The count varies: an external visitor answers five, a NiCE employee answers more, because the branch asking who they are preparing for is only reachable for them.
